The enterprise-wide plan sets total proposed funding at $503.6 million against total proposed expenditures of $509.7 million, with property tax revenue of $259.9 million budgeted to increase 3.7%, or $9.3 million. The largest single appropriation is the PA-18 special education base distribution to local districts, budgeted at $183,872,500.

**What it is**
Oakland Schools (Oakland ISD) Original Budget and five-year forecasts for fiscal year 2025-26, dated 04.01.2025. Oakland Schools is one of 56 Michigan intermediate school districts established in 1962 and serves 28 constituent districts. State law requires the ISD board to submit its proposed budget to each constituent district board no later than May 1 and to adopt no later than June 30 for the year beginning July 1.

**Enterprise-wide funding and use of resources (FY 2025-26 proposed)**

| Funding source | Amount | Expenditure category | Amount |
|---|---|---|---|
| Property taxes | $259.9 million | Salary, wage and benefits | $87.1 million |
| Other local and investment revenue | $48.0 million | Purchased services, supplies, utilities, dues/fees | $25.6 million |
| State source revenue | $24.7 million | Capital outlay | $17.8 million |
| Other financing sources and indirect | $14.0 million | Transfers to LEAs and other funds | $218.8 million |
| Estimated grant award funding | $157.0 million | Grant related expenditures | $157.0 million |
| **Total funding** | **$503.6 million** | Payment on existing debt | $3.4 million |
| | | **Total expenditures** | **$509.7 million** |

**Revenue assumptions**
Property taxes are budgeted to rise 3.7% district-wide, from $250,646,100 to $259,920,000, an increase of $9,273,900; Oakland County taxable values are expected to rise just over 4.0% but a conservative estimate was used. The tax base is 70% principal residence and 30% non-principal residence, and the District experienced a Headlee rollback in eight of the last nine years. Investment revenue falls from $8,876,900 to $7,535,100. Other local revenue moves from $40,731,400 to $40,505,200. State source revenue drops from $27,335,100 to $24,658,900 as Sections 147a(3), 147a(4), 147c(2) and 147g are removed. Grant revenue is budgeted at $156,990,000 versus $175,559,400.

**Fund-level budgets**

| Fund | FY 2025-26 revenue | FY 2025-26 expenditures | Ending fund balance |
|---|---|---|---|
| General Education (100) | $27,169,800 | $26,343,000 | $12,888,900 total; $3,951,500 unassigned (15%) |
| Special Education (200) | $209,356,700 | $209,360,600 | $21,193,800 total; $1,152,000 restricted (5%) |
| Career Focused Education (600) | $55,806,600 | $56,050,900 | $4,647,100 total; $4,618,000 restricted (8%) |
| Shared Services & Tuition (270) | $20,541,600 | $20,562,300 | $5,156,200 |
| ONE Fund (271) | $1,589,300 | $1,238,900 | $14,377,000 committed |
| Medicaid (273) | $16,328,500 | $16,328,500 | $1,200 non-spendable |
| HR/Finance Consortium (277) | $1,374,900 | $1,305,400 | $840,000 committed |

**Personnel**
Staffing rises from 640.0 to 641.4 FTE, a net 1.3 FTE increase: 1.0 FTE Senior HR Generalist, 1.0 FTE split-funded Universal Design for Learning Consultant, and a 0.7 FTE reduction in part-time staff. A 2.0% across-the-board increase plus step increases are budgeted; the collective bargaining agreement expires June 30, 2027. The blended MPSERS retirement rate is 28.56%; the most common plan rate falls from 31.36% to 29.91% on October 1, 2025, while the UAAL stabilization rate rises from 10.58% to 15.02%.

**Notable items**
A $1,000,000 placeholder Artificial Intelligence budget is created in the General Education Fund. The PA-18 base distribution to local districts grows approximately $10.3 million, or 5.9%, to $183,872,500. Michigan Tax Tribunal reserves are set at .25% of tax revenues, roughly $649,800. Board Policy 3230 subsidies total $1,364,800. Oakland Schools Technical Campus Phase II corridor refresh and parking lot replacement are to be completed during Summer 2025.
2025_309_fy26_complete_budget_external.verbose:
Oakland Schools' Original Budget for fiscal year 2025-26, date-stamped 04.01.2025 and provided to constituent district boards, including Troy School District, for review and comment. Oakland Schools is one of 56 Michigan intermediate school districts established in 1962 and serves 28 constituent districts.

ENTERPRISE-WIDE. Proposed total funding is $503.6 million: property taxes $259.9 million; other local and investment revenue $48.0 million; state source revenue $24.7 million; other financing sources and indirect revenue $14.0 million; estimated grant award funding $157.0 million. Proposed total expenditures are $509.7 million: salary, wage and benefits $87.1 million; purchased services, supplies, utilities and dues/fees $25.6 million; capital outlay $17.8 million; transfers to LEAs and other funds $218.8 million; grant related expenditures $157.0 million; payment on existing debt $3.4 million. Both are net of eliminated Risk Related Activity Fund amounts.

PROPERTY TAXES. Revenue is budgeted to increase 3.7%, or $9.3 million, with Oakland County taxable values expected to rise just over 4.0% and having reached pre-recession levels in 2022-23. By fund: General Education $14,892,100 to $15,443,100; Special Education $189,424,900 to $196,433,600; Career Focused Education $46,329,100 to $48,043,300; total $250,646,100 to $259,920,000 (+$9,273,900). The tax base is 70% principal residence and 30% non-principal residence, with a Headlee rollback in eight of the last nine years. Michigan Tax Tribunal reserves are set at .25% of tax revenues, approximately $649,800.

INITIATIVES. OSTC Phase I secured entrances and Welcome Centers are complete; Phase II corridor refresh and parking lot replacement with security gates finish in Summer 2025. A $1 million placeholder Artificial Intelligence budget (new location 031) is created in the General Education Fund. Mental health work spans Section 31n and 31p funding, the Aspire Program with New Oakland Family Services, and consultation with Oxford Community Schools; as of March 17, 2025, 499 educators had completed PREPaRE workshop 1 (23 of 28 districts) and 368 workshop 2 (28 of 28), and as of March 1, 2025, BTAM training had reached 557 educators from 22 districts plus 26 resource officers while 252 had taken suicide-prevention training developed with Dr. Steven Brock. Also funded: the Business Office Residency Program begun June 2024 with a cohort of four; the Human Resources Leadership Academy launched 2024-25; Literacy Essentials Oakland (established 2019-20), funded up to $5 million; and the EPIC numeracy initiative running PDSA cycles in 13 classrooms across 12 schools and 10 districts. The MiPEER HR/Finance Consortium, created FY 2012-13, unites 20 districts on BusinessPlus with an 18-member team. The NAIS lab at the Southeast Technical Campus (2.0 FTE consultants added 2024-25) opens fully in 2027-28; the STEMi mobile classroom, deployed 2021, is booked at all 28 districts and public school academies; 92 county schools join Michigan Green Schools; Technology Services supports 15 districts; Medicaid Billing Services should generate about $15.6 million for LEAs. Board Policy 3230 subsidies: Xello $360,000; CDX Automotive $31,400; Nepris $250,000; Alumni Pathways-Lightcast $45,000; Illuminate DnA $354,700; Discovery Education Streaming $77,600; Atlas Rubicon $199,500; STAMP $46,600; total $1,364,800.

PERSONNEL. Staffing moves from 640.0 to 641.4 FTE, a net 1.3 FTE increase: 1.0 FTE Senior HR Generalist overlapping the HR Manager position until its elimination at the end of 2025-26, 1.0 FTE Universal Design for Learning Consultant split between District & School Services and Special Populations, and a 0.7 FTE part-time reduction. A 2.0% across-the-board increase plus step increases are budgeted; the collective bargaining agreement expires June 30, 2027. Eight MPSERS rates apply; Basic/MIP with Health Care Premium Subsidy is 31.36% through September 30, 2025 and 29.91% from October 1, 2025, while the UAAL stabilization rate rises from 10.58% to 15.02%; the budgeted blended rate is 28.56%, or $28.56 per $100 of wages. Health care hard caps, reflecting House Bill 6058's 7% increase and 4.5% medical CPI growth, are $22,523.34 family / $17,271.14 individual-plus-one / $8,258.54 single after 1/1/25 and $23,536.89 / $18,048.34 / $8,630.17 after 1/1/26, with employees contributing about 18% on average. District-wide, salary and wages with FICA move from $53,278,600 to $55,710,900; MPSERS retirement costs $21,703,000 to $21,886,800; healthcare insurance $7,198,600 to $7,417,900; other insurances $2,165,200 to $2,125,100; purchased services/supplies/other $24,513,800 to $25,645,500; capital outlay $21,143,800 to $17,748,000; other financing uses $224,988,800 to $218,757,100; debt service $3,388,900 to $3,387,200 ($1,610,000 principal, $1,777,200 interest).

POLICY AND ALLOCATION. Policies 3050, 3100, 3150 and 3170 govern preparation, amendment, fund balance and transfer authority, with amendments at least three times a year. Fund balance targets are 7.5%-12.5% of operating expenditures for the General Education Fund unassigned and Career Focused Education restricted balances and 5%-10% for Special Education net of LEA transfers. General allocation is 50% General Education / 25% Special Education / 25% Career Focused Education; revenue-generating pools 70/15/15; FTE-based 24/24/52; space utilization 50/24/26; transportation miles 73/25/2; property tax millage 6% / 75.5% / 18.5%. Allocated departments total $28,663,400 ($12,665,100 Fund 100, $6,910,400 Fund 200, $9,087,900 Fund 600), or 11.15%. Cited statutes are PA 206 of 1893 (MCL 211.24e), PA 2 of 1968, and PA 451 of 1976 (MCL 380.624, MCL 380.684); the ISD board must submit its proposed budget to constituent district boards no later than May 1.

GENERAL EDUCATION FUND (100). Revenue of $27.2 million — property taxes $15.4 million (57% of total), other local $4.1 million, state $7.0 million, other financing $0.7 million — against $26.3 million of expenditures: General Administration $3.0 million, Finance and Operations $10.6 million, Instructional Programs and Services $10.6 million, Plant and Fixed Charges $2.1 million. Line totals are $27,169,800 revenue (FY 2024 actual $27,234,539; FY 2025 Amendment 2 $27,821,800) and $26,343,000 expenditure (FY 2024 actual $21,131,961; FY 2025 Amendment 2 $28,175,500), an operating surplus of $826,800. Section 81 General Aid is $4,572,600 and Section 147c(1) UAAL Rate Stabilization $1,577,100. Ending equity is $12,888,900: $8,882,100 assigned, $3,951,500 unassigned (15% of budgeted expenditures), $55,300 non-spendable. Footnotes cite a one-time $150,000 CTN distribution and a MAISA Educator on Loan agreement in 2024-25. The forecast assumes property tax growth of 3.0% in 2026-27 and 2.6% for 2027-28 through 2030-31, a 1.3% step-driven salary growth rate plus 2% base increases, a 7.65% FICA rate on wages up to $176,100 for calendar 2025, 4.0% medical CPI, and 2%-3% growth in supplies and dues; unassigned fund balance is forecast at $4.8 million (18.3%), $5.2 million (19.1%), $5.1 million (17.8%), $4.5 million (15.3%) and $3.6 million (11.9%) across 2026-27 through 2030-31. Fund 105 grant activity is $94,840,000.

SPECIAL EDUCATION FUND (200). Revenue of $209.4 million — property taxes $196.4 million (94% of total), other local $3.2 million, state $9.5 million, other financing $0.3 million — and expenditures of $209.4 million: Program Supervision and Direction $2.7 million, Program Operations $12.1 million, Plant and Fixed Charges $8.3 million, PA-18 Distribution $183.9 million, LEA Transfers and Program Subsidies $2.4 million. Line totals are $209,356,700 and $209,360,600, a $3,900 deficit. The PA-18 base distribution is $183,872,500, up approximately $10.3 million or 5.9%; the 2024-25 budget held a $9.8 million supplemental distribution of which $5.6 million went to districts in December 2024. Another $2,450,000 covers group home and medical support, incarcerated youth, startup assistance, extraordinary contingency, assistive technology and Section 24 payments. Ending equity is $21,193,800: $20,000,000 restricted for center facility renovations, $1,152,000 restricted (5%), $41,800 non-spendable. Roughly 25,100 students have an IEP. Forecast LEA base distributions are $188,623,200, $192,979,500, $197,470,200, $202,113,600 and $206,953,100 for 2026-27 through 2030-31; capital outlay is flat at $113,400. Fund 205 grant activity is $60,155,000.

CAREER FOCUSED EDUCATION FUND (600). Revenue of $55.8 million — property taxes $48.0 million (86% of total), other local $1.5 million, state $6.3 million — against $56.1 million of expenditures: Campus Operations $25.1 million, District & Campus Support Operations $4.5 million, LEA Transfers & Program Subsidies $6.3 million, Plant & Fixed Charges $20.2 million. Line totals are $55,806,600 and $56,050,900, a $244,300 deficit. FY 2026 campus totals are Northwest $5,810,300, Southeast $6,139,900, Northeast $6,893,600, Southwest $6,243,500, together $25,087,300. Eighteen state CTE program codes are listed, from 501 Agriculture to 595 Computer Programming; CTE staffing falls 0.3 FTE. The Oakland County Sheriff's Department provides one School Resource Officer per campus, fully locally funded from 2026-27. Regional programs total $4.4 million annually, STEMi operations $498,300, LEA transportation reimbursement $1.8 million. Ending restricted balance is $4,618,000 (8%), forecast at $4.1 million (7.0%), $4.5 million (7.7%), $4.5 million (7.6%), $6.7 million (11.3%) and $8.3 million (13.5%) through 2030-31.

OTHER FUNDS. Shared Services & Tuition Programs Fund 270: $20,541,600 revenue, $20,562,300 expenditure, ending $5,156,200; VLAC K-8 at 240 FTE ($6,450 resident / $6,650 non-resident), VLAC 9-12 at 250 FTE ($6,700 / $6,900) and ACE at 290 students ($4,900), all unchanged from 2024-25, plus Graduation Alliance and a KCK, Inc. foreign exchange program for about 30 students. ONE Fund 271, a fiber network of twenty-nine consortium members: $1,589,300 revenue, $1,238,900 expenditure including $300,000 each for Literacy Essentials Oakland and the Numeracy Initiative, ending committed $14,377,000; a $1.9 million infrastructure update finishes by June 30, 2025. Medicaid Fund 273: $16,328,500 in and out, transferring $13,303,400 of service fees, $1,412,800 of outreach fees and $859,600 of Caring 4 Students fees to LEAs. HR/Finance Consortium Fund 277: $1,374,900 revenue, $1,305,400 expenditure, ending committed $840,000; $4,875,000 was transferred net from the CPDI Fund in FY 2012-13 through FY 2015-16 and a $0.7 million ONE Fund startup grant repaid through 2023-24. School Activities Fund 290: $180,000 in and out, balance $257,400. Debt Service Fund 311 (2016 Refunding Bonds refunding the 2007 CFE Campus Renovation Bonds, unrefunded balance paid off May 2017) runs through 2036 at about $3.3 million a year, ending restricted at $9,898,900 after $1,610,000 principal and $852,200 interest. Fund 313 (2010 QSCB) ends at $477,400 after a $770,000 transfer to Fund 314, which takes a $762,700 federal interest subsidy, pays $925,000 term bond interest and ends at $12,888,800 before 2027 maturity. Capital Projects Fund 404: $7,262,000 revenue including a $6,700,000 CFE transfer, $12,730,400 expenditure including $4,921,900 of parking lot and gate access work and $3,312,500 of Phase II construction, ending $7,980,500. Fund 406 (Administration Building): $761,100 revenue, $3,358,100 expenditure including $1,507,900 of roof replacement, ending $10,560,700. Production Print Enterprise Fund 710: $1,060,400 operating revenue, $1,056,700 expense, ending net position $(893,800) after retroactive GASB 68 and 75; external print services drop to $350,000 as the shop refocuses on districts. Risk Related Activity Fund 810: $10,838,600 revenue, $10,716,500 expense, $122,100 net operating profit, $3,100,500 ending net position, with $1,240,000 professional liability and $1,278,400 cyber liability claim fluctuation reserves; compensated absence accruals total $3,496,500 and GASB 101 is being implemented for the year ending June 30, 2025.

CAPITAL PLAN AND CONTACTS. The five-year capital outlay plan for school fiscal years 2025-34, presented for first reading April 1, 2025, shows $92,867,300 of FY25-FY30 needs, $42,100,000 of transfers, and a projected 6/30/2030 shortfall of $(6,992,300); annual grand totals are $22,233,100, $22,322,100, $11,036,800, $14,908,500, $16,727,900 and $5,638,900. Fund 404 carries $17,235,200 of 2025-26 needs and $72,735,300 across FY25-FY30 against $39,700,000 of transfers; Fund 406 carries $3,402,900 and $10,538,200 against $2,400,000.
